whyNotReceipted: Isolation, not certification. It explains a residual; it certifies no stop. Same measured-and-not-receipted pattern as the two artifacts beside it.
phase: H3B -- isolate the second-order residual of typography.scale
conclusion: AN INLINE WRITE APPLIED TO A LIVE PAGE LEAVES SOME ELEMENTS COMPUTED AGAINST THE OLD ROOT. The same write applied BEFORE FIRST PAINT agrees with the stylesheet arm exactly. The residual is therefore a property of live mutation, not of the cascade, not of the serving model, and not of the design system.

decisiveComparison.note: Three modes, one scene, one bundle, the SAME single declaration --ds-type-scale: 0.94. Only the delivery differs.
decisiveComparison.reading: Every value agrees across the three modes except space-modern-preset-gap: 14.1px on both fresh modes and 14.6796px on the live one. Delivering the inline write on a fresh page removes the divergence WITHOUT changing the arm position.

fableHint.confirmed: The rem root IS type-scale derived: runtime/engines/classic/theme.css:22 sets html[data-tenant] { font-size: var(--ds-font-size-base) } and --ds-font-size-base is calc(0.9375rem * var(--ds-type-scale,1)). Root computes 15px at scale 1 and 14.1px at 0.94, which is why gaps and titles move at all.
fableHint.refuted: The hint predicted the root re-derives on the static arm and NOT on the inline arm. Measured: the root moves to 14.1px on BOTH arms, in the probe run too (card-modern-md/root reads 15px -> 14.1px on the DB arm after H-3a). So a root that fails to re-derive is not the explanation.

whatTheResidualActuallyIs.shape: PARTIAL AND STABLE recalculation, not a phase lag. In the probe run the DB arm reads card-modern-md/root at 14.1px (it picked up the new root) while card-modern-md/title reads 12.3375px = 13.125 x 0.94, which is the title calc applied to the OLD 15px root. One element updated, its descendant did not, in the same reading.
whatTheResidualActuallyIs.whyStableDefeatedTheH3aLaw: The H-3a stability law accepts a reading that agrees with itself under provocation. This state DOES agree with itself: measured here across two explicit invalidations, the values never changed. A stability law cannot detect a page that has stopped recalculating in the wrong place.

answerToTheBriefQuestion4: (b), a missing application on the DB arm -- and located: it is the LIVE MUTATION, not the arm position and not the serving model. This matters for scope: phase (a) of H-3 (serving the compiled artifact) is NOT required to fix it, so phase (a) stays a fidelity decision and does not come back through the back door as a symptom cure.
proposedClosure: Deliver the DB arm inline write on a FRESH page -- the write is installed before first paint and the phase is navigated, exactly as the static arm already navigates per phase. The arm keeps its production-preview position (root inline style); what changes is that nothing is computed twice. Falsifiable: typography.scale must go to ZERO divergent rows with the serving model unchanged, and the 36 stored scenarios must stay invariant by value.
radius: Every control measured through the DB arm whose witness is a rem-derived or root-inherited property is exposed to this, which is why five closed controls were unaffected: their painted witnesses did not depend on the root font-size. The invariance re-run of H-3a (36 scenarios, 26212 shared keys, zero moved) is the measured evidence that they were not.
